messages:
kevin: Heads-up — onboarding run against `mosaic-xxl` showed a weird gap. Golden smoke (10 short prompts) passed but a >2k token replay from prod fails with repeated hallucinations and KV cache blowups. Posting snippets.
anya: ugh. Are the failing cases all long-context or specific ops?
mohit: long-context + some multi-turn stateful prompts, right? saw similar with n_head_sanity mismatch last month.
kevin: yeah mostly long-context. example trace: 
```
ERROR runtime: kv-cache-mispredict at step 1823; output: <repetition loop>\nmodel: mosaic-xxl-1.0
sequence_len: 2048 -> runtime truncated to 1024
```
kevin: onboarding bench used our default smoke set (<=512 tokens) so it didn't catch it.
tia: this is exactly the "coverage gap" we talked about in the RFC followup. We need a small change to the intake gates: add a coverage map + a lightweight long-context replay.
anya: proposed minimal additions: (1) coverage-map per-model that records sequence-length buckets and token-op mix, (2) a tiny prefix-synthesis fuzzer that generates 3 deterministic long prompts per bucket, (3) a single-shot runtime dry-run of 1-2 sequences with KV telemetry.
mohit: that buys signal but increases cost. How do we keep it bounded for 100s of incoming models?
tia: make it conditional: enabled only when model claims >1k max_seq OR when architecture is novel (new attention variant). Also run on a sampled subset (1:10) for normal submissions and 1:1 for enterprise/private.
kevin: seems reasonable. also we should define the validator contract so the runtime teams can implement hook. I suggest a compact JSON response from the validator: `{\n  "compatibility_score": 0-100,\n  "fail_signatures": ["kv_mispredict","oom_kv"],\n  "suggested_mode": "serve-with-quant-fallback"\n}`
anya: add `sample_artifact` that contains the failing input id + minimal repro so we can triage offline. e.g., `sample_artifact: s3://onboard/artifacts/2955556666/repro-1.json`.
mohit: about interface boundaries: runtime teams want minimal coupling. The validator should be an async job that writes a verdict file, not a blocking API call. Gate coordinator polls status. Keep schema stable: versioned `validator_v` field.
tia: +1. Also add a lightweight checksum/fingerprint of the model graph (e.g., `fp: sha1(ops||shapes)`) so we only rerun heavy tests when fingerprint changes.
kevin: operational concerns: we need to surface these coverage gaps in the console (per-model heatmap). UX request: heatmap rows = buckets (<=512, 513-1024, 1025-2048, >2048), cols = signal types (latency, kv_err, output-divergence).
anya: I'll mock up a small proto for the coverage map and the validator verdict schema.
mohit: follow-up tradeoff: do we accept partial passes (score >= 70) with a runtime fallback policy or block until 90? My vote: allow >=70 with enforced fallback (e.g., pin to short-seq variant + degrade features).
tia: agree. Add automatic rollout policy: canary at 5% traffic with monitor for `kv_mispredict` spikes. If spike > 2x baseline, rollback.
kevin: sounds like an action list: 1) anya proto for schema, 2) tia add fingerprint + sampling policy, 3) mohit estimate costs for sampled long-replay, 4) infra to surface heatmap in console. I'll open follow-up issues.
ingest-bot: ingest pipeline run 2955556666: initial smoke ok, long-replay scheduled (est cost 0.12 credits).
anya: thanks — will post schema in #eng-ml RFC thread tomorrow. quick note: put examples in `tests/golden/long-context/` so bench infra can reuse.
kevin: perfect. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. :eyes:
